chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a free man who killed a slave whose value was twenty thousand dirhams, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible that the value of a slave exceeds the blood money (diyah) of a free man.'

key_terms.دِيَةِ: Blood money (compensation for death or injury)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum compensation for killing a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the upper limit of *diyah* (blood money) for a slave, establishing that it cannot exceed the standard compensation for a free man, thereby preventing the valuation of a slave's life from surpassing that of a free person. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that while a slave's status is distinct, their financial compensation in cases of homicide is capped to maintain equity in legal liabilities. The principle underscores the balance between social hierarchy and justice in Islamic inheritance and compensation laws.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a free man who kills a slave who value is twenty thousand Dirham. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not allowed that the value of a slave should be more than the wergild of a free’.
